Mini Sudoku 6×6 vs Sudoku 9×9 — how to choose

Compare NoCharge’s fixed Mini Sudoku 6×6 and Sudoku 9×9 boards by grid size, box shape, controls, and what is not saved.

By NoCharge Editorial·Reviewed by NoCharge Editorial·Published August 27, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read

Bottom line: The current V2 Sudoku pages offer a fixed 6×6 puzzle and a fixed 9×9 puzzle. They use the same row, column, and box rule, but differ in grid density and the available coordinate controls.

Current boards and controls

FeatureMini SudokuSudoku 9×9
Grid6×69×9
Box shape3 columns × 2 rows3×3
Digits1–61–9
EntryChoose a cell, then use the number pad or Clear cellChoose a cell, optionally set row and column, then use the number pad or Clear cell
Puzzle sourceFixed board and bundled solutionFixed board and bundled solution
Pencil marks, difficulty labels, saved resumeNot provided in current V2Not provided in current V2

How to choose

Choose the six-by-six board when you prefer fewer cells and six symbols per unit. Choose the nine-by-nine board when you want the familiar 1–9 format and do not mind a denser grid. This is a difference in board size, not a published difficulty rating or session-time promise.

What the game checks

Both pages lock the given clues and reject entries that repeat in the selected row, column, or box. The bundled answer is also used to count entries that differ from the intended solution. A wrong entry does not create a saved loss record.

Neither game has pencil marks, difficulty labels, a solver/reveal tool, or a board that persists after reload. The current state and Checks counter live in the page session; reset restores the same puzzle. NoCharge V2 does not save solved counts or local bests.
